title: Bilal on the hot sand
hookLine: an enslaved man is tortured under a rock in the midday sun, and says only one word: One

cards: Midday in Mecca, in summer, when the sand burns through your sandals. An enslaved man named Bilal is dragged out and laid on his back.
His owner has a huge rock placed on his chest, so he can barely breathe, and says: you'll stay like this until you die, or until you deny Muhammad and worship al-Lat and al-'Uzza. Bilal can't move.
He can hardly draw breath. And over and over, all he says is one word. Ahad.

teach.b: Bilal ibn Rabah was born into slavery in Mecca; his mother was from Abyssinia, across the Red Sea.
His owner, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, was one of the chiefs of Quraysh, and the biography by Ibn Ishaq tells the scene you just heard. Why that word?

teach.h: SAY: HE IS ALLAH, THE ONE!
teach.b: Ahad, One, is at the heart of a short surah, the hundred and twelfth, in Pickthall's words: “Say: He is Allah, the One!” Tawhid, day ten of this path, squeezed into a single word by a man with one breath to spend.
It's quiet defiance, too: his owner owned his body, but not that word. And the story doesn't end on the sand. Abu Bakr came by, saw what was being done, bought Bilal from Umayyah and set him free.
Years later, when the Muslims needed someone to call the people to prayer, they chose Bilal's voice.

teach.h: FREED, AND THEN THE FIRST ADHAN.
teach.b: The first adhan, day fifteen of this path, when you first heard a word from him, was called by the man who had once said Ahad under a rock. Early Mecca was cruel to the powerless who believed.
A woman named Sumayyah, tortured with her family, was killed for her faith; Muslims remember her as the first martyr of Islam.
Her son 'Ammar, under torture, said what his tormentors demanded, and came to the Prophet ﷺ in tears.
And the Qur'an says that one who is forced, while his heart stays firm in faith, is not blamed. Islam honors Bilal's courage, and it does not demand that everyone be Bilal.
That closes week thirteen: a cave, a word, a blanket, an old cousin, the morning light, as-sabiqun, and one word on the burning sand.

how: Muslims honor Bilal as the first mu'adhdhin, and many mosques and schools are named for him; his word, ahad, is remembered as a picture of steadfast tawhid.

o: a cry for help, like 'save me'
One: God is one, with no partner
the word for patience under pain

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: bought Bilal and set him free

s: Bilal was freed by his owner after he gave up
he never gave up; Abu Bakr bought him and set him free.
he was chosen as the first mu'adhdhin.
Islam blames anyone who says forbidden words under torture
the Qur'an excuses one who is forced while his heart stays firm in faith (16:106).

games.q: you're Bilal, pinned under a rock on the burning sand. your owner says: deny Muhammad, and it stops. what do you say?
o: say what he wants, just to breathe.
games.why: he repeats only ahad, ahad: One, One (Ibn Ishaq). and the Qur'an also says one forced under torture, with faith firm in the heart, is not blamed (16:106).

practice: Rest a hand flat on your chest and press gently, enough to feel it as you breathe.
Choose one word to hold on to: if you pray, Bilal's word, ahad, One; if not, a word you want to keep when things push on you, like steady, or true, or someone's name.
Say it silently with each breath, against the gentle weight of your hand.

wordCard.voice: Ahad, One: the single word Bilal repeated under the rock on the burning sand, refusing to deny it.

orig.note: Arabic: one, the only one; the word of Surah 112:1.

carryVoice: Your line: ahad, ahad. Tomorrow, the believers flee across the sea to a just king. Thirteen weeks on the path.

sources.q: Say: He is Allah, the One!
